title: Türkiye in October: Golden Autumn, Mesopotamia & Hiking Perfection
seoTitle: Türkiye in October: Mesopotamia, Hiking & Autumn
metaDescription: Plan Türkiye in October for Göbeklitepe, Mardin, and Lycian Way hiking, warm southern sea swimming, Yedigöller foliage, and beach-club closing dates.
quickAnswer: Turkey in October is the year's premier month for cultural touring and long-distance hiking. Daytime heat across Göbeklitepe, Mardin, and Gaziantep drops into the comfortable mid-20s°C, the Lycian Way opens up for full-day treks, southern Mediterranean water stays warm for swimming, and northern forests turn gold across Yedigöller and Artvin.
category: Inner Pages — 20 Month-by-Month & Seasonal Türkiye Guides

body.text: Why is October the #1 month for Göbeklitepe, Mardin, Gaziantep and Lycian Way hiking?

October breaks summer's extreme heat across Southeastern Anatolia and the Taurus foothills without bringing winter rain. Şanlıurfa drops more than 11°C from its July highs into pleasant sightseeing weather, while coastal pine trails along the Lycian Way cool enough for 12- to 18-kilometre day hikes with clear Mediterranean views.

Official [Turkish State Meteorological Service (MGM) data for Şanlıurfa](https://www.mgm.gov.tr/veridegerlendirme/il-ve-ilceler-istatistik.aspx?k=H&m=SANLIURFA) records an average October high of 27.7°C and overnight lows of 15.8°C, turning exposed archaeological walks at Göbeklitepe, Karahantepe, and the stone alleys of Old Mardin into comfortable full-day outings. In Gaziantep, mild autumn evenings make walking between pistachio markets, copper workshops, and the Zeugma Mosaic Museum effortless. Along the southwest coast, the roughly 540-kilometre [Lycian Way](https://goturkiye.com/walking/lycian-way) from Ölüdeniz to Geyikbayırı enters its prime autumn window—as detailed in the [GoTürkiye Lycian Way guide](https://goturkiye.com/culturaljourneys/lycian-way)—allowing hikers to link Patara, Kaş, Simena, and Olympos without July's dehydration risk.
Is the sea in Antalya, Kaş and Fethiye still warm enough to swim in October?

Yes—throughout October, sea surface temperatures along Antalya, Kaş, and Fethiye stay comfortably warm, averaging 23–25°C well into the final week of the month. Because Mediterranean water retains summer heat far longer than the air, midday swims after morning hikes or boat trips feel refreshing rather than cold.

Even in late November, live observations on the [MGM Piri Reis Sea Water portal](https://pirireis.mgm.gov.tr/deniz-suyu-sicakliklari) still register 21.8°C in Fethiye, 22.0°C in Finike, and 22.8°C in Kemer—confirming how reliably swimmable October stays along the Turquoise Coast. Further north on the Aegean around Bodrum and Alaçatı, early October remains pleasant for swimming, though cooler northern breezes and shorter afternoons make late October better suited to coastal walks and vineyard lunches than all-day beach lounging.
Where are the best autumn foliage spots (Yedigöller, Artvin, Cappadocia)?

Yedigöller National Park in Bolu, Artvin's Borçka Karagöl and Şavşat valleys in the northeast, and Cappadocia's poplar-lined river canyons deliver Türkiye's richest October colour. Peak foliage shifts from mid-October at higher eastern elevations to late October and early November in the western Black Sea beech forests.

Halfway between Istanbul and Ankara, [Yedigöller (Seven Lakes) National Park](https://goturkiye.com/blog/turkiye-a-winter-wonderland) layers beech, oak, hornbeam, and alder across seven landslide lakes—visit midweek to avoid weekend day-trip traffic from Istanbul. In the far northeast, Artvin's [Borçka Karagöl and Macahel](https://goturkiye.com/routes/discover-the-black-sea-highlands-in-2-weeks) frame crimson and amber mountain slopes around still crater water. In Central Anatolia, yellow poplars and turning vineyards illuminate Ihlara Valley and Red Valley against Cappadocia's pale volcanic tuff, while the [MuseumPass Türkiye](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-MSP01-27-009) streamlines entry across regional open-air museums.
When do seasonal coastal beach clubs begin closing?

Most high-season beach clubs in Bodrum, Alaçatı, and Çeşme wind down between October 10 and October 25, with final closing weekends typically timed around Türkiye's October 29 Republic Day holiday. By contrast, year-round towns like Antalya, Fethiye, and Kaş keep core hotels, restaurants, and boat operators open through late October.
Plan around seasonal transitions with this October checklist:

items: Check exact closing dates: Confirm beach-club, boutique hotel, and ferry timetables in Bodrum and Alaçatı if travelling after October 15.
Book Republic Day early: Domestic flights and boutique hotels across Cappadocia, Mardin, and Yedigöller spike in demand around October 29 (Cumhuriyet Bayramı).
Reserve Southeast hotels ahead: Historic stone mansions in Old Mardin have small room counts and sell out quickly in October.
Pack smart layers: Combine swimwear and trail shorts with a packable down vest or fleece for 6–10°C mornings in Cappadocia and Bolu.

faq.q: Is October a good month to visit Istanbul?
faq.a: Yes. October offers mild 18–22°C days in Istanbul with smaller museum queues than September, though you should pack a compact umbrella for occasional autumn showers.

faq.q: Do hot air balloons fly in Cappadocia in October?
faq.a: Yes. October is one of the strongest months for Cappadocia balloons, pairing crisp dawn air with clear visibility, though morning temperatures near 5–8°C require a warm jacket and hat.

faq.q: Can I visit Bodrum in late October?
faq.a: You can enjoy quiet coastal walks, Bodrum Castle, and year-round seafood restaurants in late October, but most seasonal beach clubs and luxury summer pop-ups close between mid-October and October 29.

faq.q: How many days do I need for Gaziantep, Şanlıurfa, and Mardin in October?
faq.a: Allow five to six full days to cover Gaziantep's culinary heritage and Zeugma Museum, Şanlıurfa's Göbeklitepe and Balıklıgöl, and Mardin's stone monasteries and Dara ruins without rushing.

faq.q: When do Turkish museums switch to winter hours?
faq.a: Ministry of Culture and Tourism sites typically shift from summer to winter operating hours in late October or November. Check individual site times before arrival via [Muze.gov.tr](https://muze.gov.tr/ETicket).

faq.q: Are mosquitoes or summer crowds still an issue on the Lycian Way in October?
faq.a: Summer tour-bus crowds drop sharply along the coast in October, while trail popularity among hikers peaks mid-month. Booking small guesthouses in Faralya, Kaş, and Çıralı a few weeks ahead secures the best rooms.
